rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: Landlords planning to end a tenancy must provide tenants with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or Notice of Lease Non-renewal. This notice must also be provided to tenants asked to leave due to property foreclosure or sale.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to end your tenancy, they must give you a special notice explaining your rights and resources at the same time they give you an eviction or non-renewal notice.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador quiere terminar su contrato de alquiler, debe darle un aviso especial que explique sus derechos y recursos al mismo tiempo que le entrega un aviso de desalojo o no renovación.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners ending tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy in Boston, except residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term treatment facilities for substance abuse.

value: non-profit short-term treatment facility for substance abuse

rules.exemptions_text: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term treatment facilities for substance abuse are exempt.

value: non-profit short-term treatment facility for substance abuse

rules.penalty: 1st offense: warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses: $300 per day fines.
rules.citation: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, Sec. 10-11.7
rules.quoted_span: The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
